Comparison

Omarchy compared with other Linux systems

Only what each official site says, with a source on every line.

Independent editorial guide

Short answer

Built on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. The tables below compare that with what each project's official site says. For CachyOS, see the longer comparison linked at the end of this page.

How this page is built

Every line below is taken from the Omarchy manual or from that project's official site. This site is not affiliated with those projects. A longer, hand written comparison for CachyOS lives on its own page.

Omarchy and Ubuntu

OmarchyUbuntu
Release modelRolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]A new version every six months; LTS releases every two years with 5 years of standard security maintenance. [ubuntu.com]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]Built on deb packages, with snap packages also supported. [ubuntu.com]
Support offerNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.Ubuntu Pro is free on up to 5 machines. [ubuntu.com]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Ubuntu facts: https://ubuntu.com/.

Omarchy and Arch Linux

OmarchyArch Linux
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]An independently developed x86-64 general-purpose distribution. [wiki.archlinux.org]
Release modelRolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]Rolling release that aims to ship the latest stable versions of most software. [wiki.archlinux.org]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]The pacman package manager, official repos for x86-64, and the community-operated AUR. [archlinux.org]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Arch Linux facts: https://archlinux.org/.

Omarchy and Fedora

OmarchyFedora
DesktopKeyboard-driven Hyprland tiling desktop. Neovim is the default editor and Foot the default terminal. [omarchy.org]Fedora Workstation features the GNOME desktop; a separate edition ships KDE Plasma. [fedoraproject.org]
VariantsNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.Atomic desktops such as Silverblue (GNOME) and Kinoite (KDE Plasma) add an extra layer of security and reliability. [fedoraproject.org]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]Fedora's software is built as RPM packages by its Koji build system. [fedoraproject.org]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Fedora facts: https://fedoraproject.org/.

Omarchy and Linux Mint

OmarchyLinux Mint
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]Based on Debian and Ubuntu, with about 30,000 packages. [linuxmint.com]
Release modelRolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]Conservative software updates; since 2014 Mint only builds on long-term support releases. [linuxmint.com]
DesktopKeyboard-driven Hyprland tiling desktop. Neovim is the default editor and Foot the default terminal. [omarchy.org]Three desktop editions: Cinnamon, MATE and Xfce. [linuxmint.com]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Linux Mint facts: https://linuxmint.com/.

Omarchy and Pop!_OS

OmarchyPop!_OS
MakerNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.Engineered and designed in-house by System76, the US computer maker. [system76.com]
DesktopKeyboard-driven Hyprland tiling desktop. Neovim is the default editor and Foot the default terminal. [omarchy.org]Auto-tiling: windows arrange themselves, adjustable by mouse or keyboard. [system76.com]
SecurityInstalls from an ISO, either full-disk or into free space next to another OS. Encryption is on by default. [omarchy.org]Full-disk encryption where only you hold the key. [system76.com]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]Any tools compatible with Ubuntu can run on Pop!_OS. [system76.com]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Pop!_OS facts: https://system76.com/pop/.

Omarchy and Bazzite

OmarchyBazzite
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]Built with Universal Blue; the KDE version is built from Fedora Kinoite and the GNOME version from Fedora Silverblue. [bazzite.gg]
UpdatesTakes a system snapshot automatically on every Omarchy update, bootable from the Limine boot menu. [omarchy.org]Image based: the previous OS version is kept after every update so you can roll back. [bazzite.gg]
Secure BootSecure Boot and/or TPM must be turned off in the BIOS to install. [omarchy.org]Secure Boot is supported, alongside SELinux and LUKS full-disk encryption. [bazzite.gg]
GamingNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.Steam and Lutris come pre-installed, with HDR and VRR support. [bazzite.gg]

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Bazzite facts: https://bazzite.gg/.
